> Hi,
>
> The ALC4080 audio solution appears to perhaps not fully comply to the
> USB Audio specification, and because of this, some features for proper
> operations under Linux such as controlling the microphone gain are not
> currently exposed.
>
> Would Realtek be so kind as to provide the required missing
> information/documentation so that the Linux community can enable the
> missing features?  I would very much like to be able to use the
> microphone input on my $400 ASUS motherboard I've recently purchased :-)
> 
> The issue is being discussed on the Linux kernel bug tracker here:
> <https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=218913>
> 
> It'd be nice if one of your engineers could drop by and provide a hint
> or two about directions to take to resolve this issue.
> 
> Thank you for taking the time to read this and for your consideration,

For anyone who want to capture their codecs too but without installing Windows on host - here some instruction to speed up this investigation.

First of all recommend to download:
1) Windows 10 (Windows 11 require UEFI) - https://www.microsoft.com/software-download/windows10ISO
2) Virtio ISO image - https://fedorapeople.org/groups/virt/virtio-win/direct-downloads/archive-virtio/ 
3) Install QEMU on host system
4) Install on HOST Wireshark using your package manager

QEMU setup
1) Create image - `qemu-img create -f qcow2 win10.qcow2 100G`
2) Run QEMU
```
sudo qemu-system-x86_64 \
    -smp 8,cores=8,threads=1,sockets=1 \
    -cpu host \
    -vga qxl \
    -machine accel=kvm \
    -m 16384 \
    -nic user,model=virtio-net-pci \
    -rtc base=localtime \
    -usb -device usb-tablet \
    -name "Windows 10" \
    -device virtio-blk-pci,drive=drive0,id=virtblk0,num-queues=8 \
    -drive file=win10.qcow2,if=none,id=drive0,format=qcow2,index=0 \
    -boot once=c,menu=on \
    -nodefaults \
    -display gtk,zoom-to-fit=off \
    -device qemu-xhci,id=xhci -device usb-host,bus=xhci.0,hostdevice=/dev/bus/usb/001/003 \
    -drive file=Win10_22H2_Ukrainian_x64v1.iso,media=cdrom,index=0 \
    -drive file=virtio-win-0.1.271.iso,media=cdrom,index=1
```

PS: `/dev/bus/usb/001/003` - you should put here your path to ALC4080
PSS: It will automatically unbind device from drivers
PSSS: Run QEMU with root permissions - it need to properly work with USB

Installation:
1) During first run it should automatically run Windows Installer
2) During installation Windows Installer should ask you where get drivers - just click to load from disk and select proper driver from Virtio ISO image
3) After installation recommend to open in Windows - Virtio ISO cdrom and open setup wizard to install all other drivers like QXL video driver and network driver and etc
4) After download into Windows driver for your ALC4080 from MB website and install it - in device manager it should be device near all other USB devices and without any warnings that this device can not be started or initialized.
5) Run on HOST - `sudo modprobe usbmon` 
6) Run on HOST Wireshark with root permissions, like `sudo wireshark` - it need to able capture USB
7) Now you will see `usbmonX`, where X it USB bus number - click on needle one
8) In filters write `usb.device_address == deviceNumber` - replace deviceNumber by actual one
9) Save your dumps in format to able it open again - I not sure what better I selected default one .pcapng

PS: Do not forget about reboots of VM
PSS: When you will capture please select proper USB for capturing - for example if your parameter for QEMU looks like this `hostdevice=/dev/bus/usb/001/003` it mean that you need to select `usbmon1` and set filter to something like that `usb.device_address == 3`
PSSS: Driver not always send to USB packets right after click - I not sure, maybe it does right before audio acting or I don't know. I mean that in case when it nothing send need trigger some acting with audio or microphone depend on option your changed - like play audio or listen microphone.

Also I think you need to records video or record all timings when you did some action to able determine it in dump.

As mentioned before by @perexg - better to report about it to https://bugzilla.kernel.org/ (it already has some issues related to microphone especially like - https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=218913 ) 

I think that should be enough.
Maybe, need simultaneously report about those issues to MB Vendors or to Realtek - maybe some of them will help with documentation or firmware updates

@pog5 I suggest to run this command during audio play and when no audio (wait at least 20-30 seconds and after run) - `pactl list sinks | grep Stat` 
In case if suspending disabled it should show `Idle` instead `Suspended` without audio and `Running` with audio
In case suspending still works it will show `Suspended` without audio after some time (please make sure you applied config on proper port - I applied for whole audio in Linux)

I also suggest to use S/PDIF port with disabled suspending - more likely you will get lower level of pops (because it will use codec inside your audio system instead of ALC4080)
If you can not use S/PDIF and suspending properly disabled on used port - you need investigate how to enable something like Fade-in effect

I though I was going insane, I had this exact same issue on my Asus ROG STRIX x870E-E. If I restarted instead of shutdown with S4+S5 ErP, the issue moved to Windows. With ErP disabled even on some shutdowns the problem moved to Windows as well, with the pop on voice calls/watching streams only on the left channel.

I also tried all your steps with no avail, had to buy an external usb card

Edit: To add more detail on the S4+S5 behavior: the pop seems to be related to a persistent hardware state in the ALC4080 that survives reboots. When shutting down without ErP (S4+S5) or restarting, the codec retains some initialization state that carries over to Windows on the next boot and the pop then appears on Windows as well, only on the left channel, during voice streams start/stop. With ErP enabled (full power cut), the codec resets completely and Windows boots clean without the pop.

Edit2: Just confirmed that even a normal shutdown (not restart) from Linux can leave the codec in a dirty state, booted into Windows after a clean shutdown and the pops were present. Powering off from Windows and booting again cleared them. This suggests the issue is specifically in how Linux de-initializes the codec at shutdown, not just on restart.

Hello.  I have a MSI Tomahawk x870e wifi motherboard with Asrock challenger 9070xt video card and have a similar issue with my audio.  I had installed CachyOS back in October with KDE plasma and have continue to update it as usual and everything worked fine.  Last week I decided to do a fresh install of the OS and went with Gnome instead of Plasma.  My setup is display port from my 9070xt to my monitor and hdmi port on the 9070xt to my sound bar just for sound. This time, no audio.  I did a few searches and found nothing that would fix the issue.  I finally went with Google's Gemini to see what AI could recommend and it brought back an interesting issue.  Apparently starting in kernel 6.19x the kernel team introduced DMI black list.  Since the Tomahawk onboard audio is seen as a usb device, the dmi black listed it. Unfortunately in my case, blocking the usb audio controller breaks all the audio devices, ie no audio from the hdmi port on the video card.  So 6.19x and 7.0x block that onboard audio controller and all the suggestions that the AI gave me could not unblock it.  The temporary solution is to use the LTS kernel which is 6.18x since this is the kernel that does not have the dmi blacklist added to it.  I can confirm this solution does work.  For those who want to test the issue, the april releases of CachyOS and EndeavourOS iso's use the 6.19x kernel for the live iso and there is no audio.  I opened a ticket and included a ALSA log file as well as my AI conversation of everything I tried.  https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=221490
So from what I can tell, since i was upgrading from an older install, going from kernel 6.17 to 6.18 to 6.19 to 7.0 there was no audio issue, but when I did a complete reinstall of the OS and it went straight to the 7.0x kernel the dmi blacklist took effect. The Key Finding
The DMUB firmware version is different:

6.18 loads 0x0A003500 for the 9070 XT
6.19 loads 0x0A000800 for the 9070 XT

0x0A003500 is actually a newer/higher version than 0x0A000800. This means kernel 6.19 is loading an older DMUB firmware than 6.18, which is backwards and almost certainly the root cause of the broken HDMI audio.
The DMUB (Display Management Unit Block) handles the display engine including HDMI audio transmission. If 6.19+ is loading an older firmware version that has a bug in its HDMI audio handling, that would explain exactly why the audio is silent despite everything else appearing correct.

Update Your Bug Report With This
This is the most concrete finding yet. Add to your bugzilla report:
Subject update: Regression: AMD 9070 XT HDMI audio silent on kernel 6.19+ due to older DMUB firmware being loaded
Key evidence:
Kernel 6.18 (working):
DMUB firmware version=0x0A003500

Kernel 6.19+ (broken, all distros):
DMUB firmware version=0x0A000800

Kernel 6.19 loads an older DMUB firmware version than 6.18
The DMUB handles HDMI audio transmission
HDA controller binding succeeds on both kernels
Raw ALSA speaker-test runs without errors but produces no audio on 6.19+
Hypothesis: the older DMUB firmware loaded by 6.19+ has a regression in HDMI audio handling for Navi 48 (device ID 0x1002:0x7550)

This is a very strong, specific, well-evidenced bug report now. The kernel developers can look directly at what changed in DMUB firmware loading between 6.18 and 6.19 for the 9070 XT.
